# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

S5 Finish parseBytes in pretty-bytes: add decimal units (kB, MB, GB, TB and the rest without the `i`) and document parseBytes in the readme. (Nov 3, 10:09 AM)
**Investigated**: The observed session read index.js, test.js, index.d.ts, index.test-d.ts and readme.md to map the parseBytes multiplier table, regex, rejection tests and documentation. It confirmed that decimal units were previously rejected by an explicit guard, and that the readme and JSDoc both described binary-only support.

**Learned**: parseBytes resolves units through PARSE_MULTIPLIERS, which previously held only binary entries. The regex accepts an optional sign, a plain decimal number, and an optional unit separated by whitespace or not at all. Tests pin the rejection contract for exponent notation, trailing decimal points, NaN, Infinity, comma separators, and non-string inputs. Git on branch storage-app shows HEAD at 647cfd7, and the strict-SI commit 69ddc6c that earlier notes mentioned does not appear in recent history.

**Completed**: parseBytes now accepts kB, MB, GB, TB, PB, EB, ZB and YB as powers of 1000, matching prettyBytes output without binary: true. KB is accepted as an alias meaning 1000 bytes. Other units remain case-sensitive, so kb, mB, Kb and K are rejected. The "Unsupported unit" error lists every accepted unit. Tests were updated to cover decimal units, unsupported units, and a round-trip with prettyBytes. The readme and index.d.ts describe both families, and the stale index.d.ts summary line was fixed. npm test reports 57 passed and 3 skipped. Changes are in index.js, test.js, index.d.ts and readme.md, and are not committed.

**Next Steps**: The observed session is wrapping up the parseBytes change. Remaining work is to confirm the uncommitted diff is what the user wants, and to decide whether to commit before anything pins the storage-app branch.

**Notes**: The KB-as-1000 choice is a judgment call that the user may want to revisit, since KB is commonly read as 1024. The branch name and the existence of commit 69ddc6c were not confirmed by git output, so any pinning service should be verified before pushing. The JSDoc has no decimal example, while the readme does.
